chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from one of his companions, who said:

Regarding a man who emancipated a mother of his children, then died from her before she had fulfilled her waiting period. He said: 'She would observe the waiting period of four months and ten (days), and if she was pregnant, she would wait with the further of the two terms'.

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child (a slave woman who bears her master's child)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a freed slave woman if her master dies before her iddah is complete?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi clarifies that emancipation does not terminate the iddah obligation upon the master's death, ensuring the woman's lineage and status are secured during the waiting period. The principle of taking the longer duration (four months and ten days or childbirth) reflects the Shia juristic preference for caution in matters of lineage and inheritance, aligning with the broader legal framework of 'iddah found in the Quran.
